key_insight: Compact multimodal language models can support pulmonary embolism risk assessment best when they combine CTPA images with EHR context, rather than using imaging alone.
clinical_relevance: This work suggests efficient AI tools may help early PE diagnosis and prognosis support, especially where structured imaging plus longitudinal clinical history are both available.
method: Built INSPECT-based benchmark with 23,248 CTPA studies from 19,402 patients.
Reframed 8 PE diagnostic and prognostic tasks as structured clinical question answering.
Compared efficient MLLMs across CTPA-only, EHR-only, and CTPA+EHR settings with zero-shot and few-shot prompting.
evidence_signal: Across evaluations, Gemma4 E4B and Gemma4 E2B performed better when EHR evidence was included, with PE diagnosis outperforming prognostic tasks overall.
watch_item: Performance was lower for prognostic tasks such as readmission prediction, so real-world use would need careful validation before clinical deployment.
paper_title: Efficient Multimodal Clinical Question Answering for Pulmonary Embolism Risk Assessment
